title: LEGO Marvel Avengers: Doomsday sets officially revealed
summary: LEGO and Marvel Studios have confirmed five new sets for Avengers: Doomsday, including a BrickHeadz pack, a Doctor Doom bust, and minifigure-based builds like the Quinjet.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Group and Marvel Studios have officially confirmed five sets tied to the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film, continuing the tradition of set waves for previous Avengers instalments.

Confirmed so far:

- **40880 Avengers: Doomsday Heroes & Villain** – a LEGO BrickHeadz pack featuring The Thing, Thor, Gambit and Doctor Doom (467 pieces, £34.99 / $39.99 / €39.99, out 4 October 2026). Notably, this is currently the only way to get a LEGO figure of the MCU version of Gambit.
- **76345 Doctor Doom Bust** – a 379-piece display bust of the film's main villain, including a textile hood and metal-effect mask, plus a Doctor Doom minifigure that also appears in other sets in the wave (£44.99 / $49.99 / €49.99, out 1 September 2026).
- **76347 Avengers: Doomsday Quinjet** – a minifigure-scale Quinjet build, seemingly for the New Avengers, with room for a pilot up front and passengers in the back (433 pieces, £54.99 / $59.99 / €59.99, out 4 October 2026).

A fourth set, **76348 Epic Battle**, is also part of the wave, alongside a further minifigure playset, though full details on these two weren't included in the available source material. The wave is also said to bring new minifigures for characters including Sentry and Red Guardian.

Most sets in the range launch on 4 October 2026, with the Doctor Doom Bust arriving slightly earlier on 1 September 2026.

## Why it matters
This marks the fifth Avengers film to get its own dedicated LEGO wave, following Avengers, Age of Ultron, Infinity War and Endgame. For MCU fans and minifigure collectors, it's a chance to finally get certain characters in physical form — including the first LEGO figure of the film's Gambit via BrickHeadz. Busts and minifigure playsets also continue to be a popular route for both display builders and collectors chasing specific characters.

## What to watch next
Full details on 76348 Epic Battle and the remaining minifigure playset in the wave haven't been confirmed yet in the material we've seen — worth checking LEGO's official channels or Brick Fanatics for the complete line-up and box art as more images and info emerge closer to release.

title: LEGO reveals Avengers: Doomsday minifigures, including Doctor Doom's return
summary: The LEGO Group has officially unveiled minifigures for its upcoming Avengers: Doomsday sets, bringing back Doctor Doom for the first time in over a decade alongside upgraded Fantastic Four figures and new X-Men characters.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The LEGO Group has officially revealed minifigures for a wave of new Marvel sets tied to Avengers: Doomsday. The lineup includes 76347 Avengers: Doomsday Quinjet (four minifigures, among them MCU-style Cyclops and a shirtless The Thing), 76348 Epic Battle: Avengers: Doomsday (six minifigures including several new X-Men characters), and 76352 Avengers Doomsday: New Avengers Tower (six minifigures covering New Avengers characters). There's also 76345 Doctor Doom Bust, which includes a second Doctor Doom variant with printed arms and fabric detailing.

Notably, Doctor Doom returns to LEGO Marvel for the first time since 76005 Spider-Man: Daily Bugle Showdown retired back in 2014 — he'll appear in both movie and comic-accurate minifigure forms, including in the 76340 LEGO Marvel Advent Calendar 2026. Mr Fantastic also gets a rework, swapping the stilt-like long-leg assembly from 76316 Fantastic Four vs. Galactus for proper minifigure legs and a more accurate face print. Printed legs feature across most of the new figures, which remains relatively uncommon for LEGO Marvel sets.

## Why it matters
This is a strong showing for LEGO Marvel collectors, with Doctor Doom's long-awaited return likely to be a highlight for anyone who's followed the theme for years. The upgraded Mr Fantastic and wider use of printed legs also suggest LEGO is investing more detail into its Marvel minifigures than in recent waves, which is good news for anyone building or displaying a Marvel collection.

## What to watch next
Expect more official details on pricing, release dates, and full set contents as Avengers: Doomsday approaches. Fans should also watch for further reveals covering additional characters across the wider wave.

## What happened

bodyMarkdown:
## What happened

Merriam revealed that controlling the barrels' speed was the toughest challenge, saying he 'rolled thousands of barrels down those tracks' during development. The team also tried various ways of returning barrels to the top, including gears and levers, before settling on a simpler solution — just using more barrels. The finished chute holds 14 barrels with room for up to 20, creating what Merriam calls an 'infinite barrel loop'.

## Why it matters
Designer insight like this gives builders a rare look at how LEGO translates classic gaming mechanics into physical, playable models.
